To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the pH of the medium and the speed of shaking of bacterial cultures are crucial factors affecting the amount of the precipitated minerals; (ii) calcium acetate is the best source of calcium ions for the mineralization process, while the temperature of cultivation does not affect the biomineral process; (iii) the presence of urease enzyme is necessary for the formation of the mineralized structure.
the highest precipitation of calcium carbonate occurs at alkaline pH between the 8-9 with shaking at 120 rpms, with the use of calcium acetate as the calcium source, in a urea-containing medium.

1) the biomineralisation process was affected by the pH and the agitation speed; 2) calcium acetate was the strongest source of calcium ions for the biomineral process; 3) the correlation between the biomineral and the cultivation temperature is not clearly defined; 4) the morphology and size of the calcium carbonate minerals were strain-specific.
